title: Shape hunt

slides.title: The Building Yard
slides.text: The street climbs to the Building Yard, where every beam must be the right shape before it can hold anything up. Tally sorts the shapes the way the yard does: by their properties, never by their looks.

slides.title: Sort by properties
slides.text: A property is something you can test: count the sides, feel for square corners, check whether sides run side by side. These four shapes differ by their counts. Test each one before you name it.

visual.label: Four drawn shapes told apart by their side counts: a triangle, a square, a pentagon and a hexagon

focus.cue: Triangle: only 3 sides, so it is no quadrilateral.
Hexagon: 6 sides, every one of them straight.

slides.title: Worked example: a family matter
slides.text: Rough first: the square probably belongs with the rectangles, because their corners match. Test the properties, not the look. A square has 4 sides and 4 square corners, and so does every rectangle.
steps: A square is a kind of rectangle

visual.label: A square and a rectangle side by side, each with 4 sides and 4 square corners marked

focus.cue: A rectangle has the same 4 square corners.
Same properties, same family: a square is a rectangle.

slides.title: Angle is a turn
slides.text: Stand and face the door. Turn a quarter turn and you face the side wall. That amount of turn is an angle, and a square corner is exactly one quarter turn. Shapes carry their turns at every corner.

slides.title: Stretch: the odd one
slides.text: Stretch: draw a quadrilateral that is not a square and not a rectangle. What properties does yours have? Stretch work is never in the check.

slides.title: Words to know
slides.text: Four words for the yard's sorting shed.

words.means: one straight edge of a shape
the point where two sides meet, and the turn between them
something true about a shape that you can test and count

slides.title: Your mission
slides.text: Open Brain Board at Practice Board and score 3,000 points to finish. It opens straight on your Shape Hunt board, and your board saves as you go. Get there your way: lots of easy tiles, or fewer hard ones. Test sides and corners before you name any family.
slides.alt: Brain Board's Shape Hunt board on a phone: a Count the sides question for 100 points, four answers to pick from.

talk: Hunt the room you are in, at home or at school: find one shape with 4 equal sides, one shape with no square corners, and one shape with 4 square corners. What family is each one in, and how do you know?
